note: Words that may not appear on a surface Daniel reads. This is the machine-readable half of docs/WRITING.md rule 4 (no house vocabulary) and rule 3 (state the fact, not a term of art for it); tools/check_writing.py reads it and CI runs the check. Adding a term here is how a writing rule stops depending on somebody noticing. Each entry: `term` is a regular expression matched case-insensitively against whole words; `means` is what it actually refers to, for whoever has to rewrite the line; `instead` is the plain wording to reach for; `hard` false means the check reports it without failing, for words that are borderline rather than wrong.
why: Daniel, 2026-09-04, reading 'Re-run the suites so each stamps the commit it proved': "What are the suites? I think it's test suites, but I don't have enough context on this page to know. 'stamps' and 'proves' are terms of art, not literal? ... We need a way to eradicate all of this hard to handle text. It's only causing friction, and the friction is so severe that it's getting in way of the process."
